metaDescription: Six countertop clear ice makers compared on cube shape, batch time, daily output and water handling, for cocktails, whiskey and slow-melting drinks.
expertTake: The EUHOMY 34 lb clear cube maker is the best pick for most bars because it combines a top tank with two ways to add water and fast batches. The Luma Comfort is the value pick for high daily volume. Skip clear ice machines if you want ice in under five minutes, because clear freezing is slow by design. Use filtered water for the clearest cubes.
introParagraphs: Clear ice looks like glass because it is frozen slowly in one direction, which pushes dissolved air and impurities away from the cube. Cloudy ice, by contrast, traps air and minerals as it freezes quickly in all directions. Clear ice melts more slowly and dilutes a drink less, which is why bars use it for whiskey and cocktails. The look and the slow melt are the reasons people pay more for it.

Countertop clear ice makers imitate that directional freezing with circulating water or spray. They cost more and run slower than bullet-ice makers, and they differ in cube shape, batch size and how you fill them. This guide compares six machines on those points. Reading batch time next to cube count tells you more than the daily figure.

products.name: EUHOMY Clear Ice Cube Maker with 1.5L Top Tank 34 lb
products.description:
The EUHOMY clear cube maker earns the top spot by combining a practical top tank with two ways to add water and fast batches for a clear machine. A 1.5 liter top tank lets you refill without moving the machine, and the ability to add water either through the tank or by another route is useful on a crowded bar.

It lists sixteen cubes in about seven minutes and a rated 34 pounds per day, which is a brisk pace for a clear-ice unit. Clear ice is made by freezing water in layers while circulation pushes bubbles and impurities away, so it takes longer than a standard bullet batch. Cubes come out clearer and denser, so they melt slowly in a glass.

Compared with the EUHOMY 45 lb, it makes fewer cubes per cycle but is quicker per batch. Compared with the Luma Comfort, it offers a top tank and fresher design. Rated output is a best case in a cool room, and a warm room cuts it. Descale regularly and use filtered water. Pour cold filtered water for the clearest result.
products.bestFor: Home bars that want fast clear cubes and easy refilling.
pros: Sixteen cubes in about seven minutes
cons: Clear ice is still slower than bullet ice

products.name: EUHOMY Ice Cube Maker 45 lb with 24 Cubes per Batch
products.description:
The 45 lb EUHOMY produces larger batches of 24 square cubes in about 13 minutes with a rated 45 pounds per day. That batch size suits parties and heavy use, though each cycle takes longer than on the 34 lb model.

Square cubes are the classic bar shape, and they stack neatly in a glass. Two ways to add water give flexibility, and a self-cleaning cycle flushes the reservoir.

Compared with the 34 lb EUHOMY, it makes more ice but takes longer per batch. Compared with the Luma Comfort, it is quicker to first cubes. Descale regularly. Keep several inches of clearance on every side so the compressor can breathe. Because each cycle is long, start the machine early in the day so the basket is full by evening. Store finished cubes in a freezer bag if the party is a day away.
products.bestFor: Hosts who make large amounts of clear ice for parties.

products.name: EUHOMY 2 Inch Ice Ball Maker 4 Pieces in 40 Minutes
products.description:
The EUHOMY ice ball maker makes four 2 inch spheres in about 40 minutes and lists up to 144 pieces per day. Spheres are the whiskey drinker's choice, since a ball has the lowest surface area for its volume and melts slowest.

The tradeoff is time. Forty minutes per batch is slow, so this machine rewards planning ahead. Compared with the cube makers, it makes far fewer pieces per cycle but each one is a showpiece.

A self-cleaning cycle flushes the reservoir, and descaling is still needed. It suits whiskey and cocktail fans. Plan the day around it: start a batch while you prepare dinner and have four spheres ready by the time guests settle in. Spheres suit rocks glasses with a wide mouth, so check that your glass fits a 2 inch ball.
products.bestFor: Whiskey drinkers who want slow-melting 2 inch spheres.

products.name: EUHOMY 2 Inch Clear Ice Cube Maker with App 110 Cubes Daily
products.description:
This EUHOMY makes 2 inch clear square cubes, two at a time in about 27 minutes, with app control and a stated 110 pieces per day. Large cubes are the bar standard for whiskey, melting slowly and chilling without dilution.

App control lets you schedule or monitor batches from a phone. Compared with the ball maker, it makes a more conventional shape. Compared with the 34 lb cube maker, it makes far fewer, larger pieces.

Smart features add complexity, so confirm it works without the app. Descale on schedule. Treat the daily figure as a ceiling that depends on room temperature. The slow two-cube cycle makes this a sipping-ice machine rather than a party machine, and the app mostly helps by letting you start a batch before you get home.
products.bestFor: Cocktail enthusiasts who want large clear cubes and app control.

products.name: Oylus Clear Ice Cube Maker 8 Jelly Cubes per Batch
products.description:
The Oylus uses spray technology to make eight crystal-clear 1.2 inch jelly cubes per batch. Spray freezing layers water onto the cold surface, which helps push air out and keeps the cubes clear.

Smaller 1.2 inch cubes fit a standard glass and cool a drink faster than a big cube, though they melt faster than 2 inch cubes. Compared with the large-cube EUHOMY, it suits everyday drinks rather than sipping.

Descale regularly and use filtered water for the clearest results. Jelly ice is a name for clear, glassy cubes that look like gelatin. Small clear cubes work well in water, iced tea and short cocktails. Wipe the cold plate gently during cleaning and avoid sharp tools. Keep the batch out of direct sun so the cubes do not melt before you use them.
products.bestFor: Everyday drinkers who want small, clear cubes.

products.name: Luma Comfort Clear Ice Cube Maker 40 lb in 24 Hours
products.description:
The Luma Comfort lists a rated 40 pounds per 24 hours with first cubes in about 15 minutes. It is the older, plain design in this guide and sits at a low-middle price tier.

Its value is volume per dollar. Compared with the EUHOMY 34 lb, it makes more ice but lacks the top tank and modern features. Compared with the Oylus, it makes larger quantities of ordinary clear cubes.

Expect to descale regularly and use filtered water, since clear ice shows impurities. Its plain design means fewer features to break but also less convenience, so you will refill from the front and scoop by hand. Pair it with a filter pitcher for the clearest ice.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want high daily volume at a low-middle tier.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Clear ice freezes slowly in one direction while circulating water or spray pushes air and impurities away. That takes longer than bullet ice, which freezes fast around prongs. Expect 7 to 40 minutes per batch. Fresh filtered or distilled water clears most cloudiness at the source. The clarity you see in a bar is the result of patience, so any machine that promises both speed and clarity deserves skepticism.

Large 2 inch cubes and spheres melt slowest and suit whiskey. Smaller 1.2 inch cubes cool faster for everyday drinks. Match the shape to your glass. A big cube can crack a thin glass if dropped, so handle with care. Check that your glass has the room for a large cube or ball before you order.

The 34 lb EUHOMY makes 16 cubes in 7 minutes, while the ball maker makes 4 in 40. A bigger batch is better for parties, slower batches for sipping. Parties favor big batches, while sipping favors slow batches. Divide the daily figure by the batch time to see how many cycles a day it really implies.

A 1.5 liter top tank and two ways to add water, as on the EUHOMY, make refilling easy. Machines that need awkward access are a daily annoyance. A reservoir you cannot easily reach is a daily annoyance.

Clear ice shows impurities. Use filtered or distilled water, and descale every month or two. Self-cleaning cycles do not remove scale. A cheap pitcher filter is the simplest upgrade. Skipping descaling clouds the cubes and shortens the life of the pump.
Compressors hum and pumps gurgle. Leave several inches of clearance and place it away from where you sleep. Keep a coaster under the machine to catch drips.

howWeEvaluated.title: Clarity method
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how each machine freezes ice from the spec sheet. Owner photos of cloudy cores informed the weighting.

howWeEvaluated.title: Batch speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed batch time against cube count. Batch time was treated as a trade, not a defect. Fast first batches mattered less than steady quality across the day.

howWeEvaluated.title: Shape and size
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched shapes to drink types. Shape suitability for the glass counted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filling and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited top tanks and weighed descaling. A top tank scored higher than a rear tank.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value by tier
howWeEvaluated.description: We ordered picks by relative price tier, from the Luma Comfort up to the app model. Cheaper machines ranked well only if the ice stayed clear.

howToChoose.intro: Match the ice to the drink, because the best machine for whiskey is not the best for volume.
Prices move, so these are relative tiers from the cheapest pick to the most expensive pick in this lineup.

cards.label: Cubes
cards.text: The EUHOMY 34 lb, 45 lb and Luma Comfort make cubes that stack well.

cards.label: Spheres
cards.text: The EUHOMY ball maker makes spheres that melt slowest.

howToChoose.note: Choose spheres for sipping, cubes for volume. Sphere makers are slower still, so plan ahead for a gathering.

howToChoose.intro: Filling is a daily chore, so compare access before output.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Large clear cubes or spheres that melt slowly and dilute little. Pre-chilled glasses also keep the ice from melting early.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The EUHOMY ball maker and the 2 inch app cube maker suit whiskey. Both give you the slow melt that sipping needs.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want large showpiece ice. The ball and app models pay off. The cost buys slow-melt shapes rather than speed.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want clear cubes in volume. The Luma Comfort covers it. Plain clear cubes are still better than cloudy ones.

maintenance.why: Scale clouds the ice and cuts output. Use citric acid and rinse well. Skipping it is the most common reason cubes turn cloudy.
It flushes the reservoir. Run it weekly to flush the lines.
Standing water grows biofilm. Prop the lid open to air out. A dry bin avoids musty smells.
The compressor needs airflow. Keep several inches clear on every side.

faq.a: It freezes directionally, which takes longer than fast freezing. It is the same effect that makes natural lake ice clear. That slow freeze is the reason clear ice costs more to make.
For whiskey and cocktails, yes. For water, less so. Soda and juice mask the difference, so use clear ice where you can taste or see it. Many owners enjoy the look as much as the performance.
Yes for the clearest results. Distilled water avoids minerals that cloud ice. Tap water in hard-water areas gives cloudy ice and white scale.
No. Ice melts slowly and drains. A cooler or freezer bag is the usual storage workaround. Move cubes to a freezer bag if you want to keep them.
They hum like a mini fridge. Place it in a spot where background noise masks the sound. Pump noise tends to be higher in clear-ice models than in plain bullet makers. Cabinets muffle it.
A 2 inch sphere or large cube. Large spheres also show up well in photographs. Surface area is the reason: less surface melts less.
